result:
**Opening argument: β(ℤ₂ × ℤ₂ⁿ) = 2ⁿ⁺¹**

**Lower bound.** Any poset with automorphism group ℤ₂ × ℤ₂ⁿ must contain an element σ of order 2ⁿ, so some σ-orbit O has size 2ⁿ. Automorphisms preserve height, so O lies at a single height and is an antichain. A single orbit of size 2ⁿ is not enough. If every other σ-orbit had size less than 2ⁿ, then elements i and i + 2ⁿ⁻¹ of O would have identical relations to every smaller orbit, since those relations depend only on the index modulo the orbit size. A transposition swapping them would then be an extra automorphism, and the group would be too large. So a second orbit of size 2ⁿ is required, giving |P| ≥ 2ⁿ⁺¹.

**Construction.** Take antichains C = {cᵢ} and D = {dᵢ}, indexed by ℤ₂ⁿ, with cᵢ < dⱼ iff j − i ∈ S. Choose S with S + 2ⁿ⁻¹ = S. The shift σ (cᵢ ↦ cᵢ₊₁, dᵢ ↦ dᵢ₊₁) and the involution τ (fixing C, dᵢ ↦ dᵢ₊₂ⁿ⁻¹) commute and generate ℤ₂ × ℤ₂ⁿ. This uses exactly 2ⁿ⁺¹ elements.

**Candid caveat.** The weakest step is the existence of S with no extra automorphisms. I assert it rather than prove it, and the lower bound's "no further symmetries" step is likewise sketched. Those are the points I'd want checked. The n ≥ 50 hypothesis also suggests the true answer may depend on n in a more delicate way, so I'd ask Debater B to identify a specific poset on fewer than 2ⁿ⁺¹ elements, or a concrete flaw in the S construction, before accepting 2ⁿ + 2.
